newsitem.title: GERMANY: German debt, futures under control of U.S. market.
newsitem.headline: German debt, futures under control of U.S. market.

text.p: German debt futures were slightly down in early dealings on Monday on follow-through selling from Friday as the market was unable to escape the U.S. Treasury market's downturn.
DTB June Bund futures were down four basis points at 100.41 points, while the 10-year benchmark 6.00 percent Bund due January 2007 was at 100.67 points, down from 100.72 on Friday.

Traders looked for the debt market to follow the influence of the U.S. market during the week, which will be shortened by Thursday's national holiday when the market will be closed, and the release of U.S. data during the week.

While only German current accounts data is expected on Tuesday, market focus will be on the release on Tuesday of durable goods ordres for March and the April consumer confidence index for any signs of inflation pressure.
Also scheduled for Tuesday is the U.S. first quarter employment cost index.
Any mounting speculation about a U.S. interest rate hike after the reports would likely weigh on the German market as well despite few concerns about German inflation, traders said.
"Any U.S. market losses would certainly weigh on us but the domestic outlook will offer some support," one trader said.
Other factors that may push German debt lower are concerns about the French and Italian debt markets.

The market generally ignored the weekend Group of Seven meeting in Washington at which Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer warned against a further rise in the dollar and said he saw no reason to change Germany's current monetary policy.
